questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What Drew Europeans to India' refers to.
questions.a: Spices, fine cotton cloth, silk and indigo pulled European merchants across the seas to India from the fifteenth century; Portuguese, Dutch, French and English companies competed for these profitable trades, fighting each other for ports and privileges.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What Drew Europeans to India'.
questions.a: India's spices and textiles were the magnet; trade rivalry was the engine of European arrival.

questions.q: Under which section is 'What Drew Europeans to India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: hees104.txt lines 20-110 (what drew European traders, age of colonialism))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The English East India Company' refers to.
questions.a: Chartered in 1600, the English East India Company built trading factories at Madras, Bombay and Calcutta, kept its own army, and used diplomacy and war to bend Indian rulers, transforming from a trading body into a territorial power.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The English East India Company'.
questions.a: A company with an army: trade posts at Madras, Bombay and Calcutta grew into an empire.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The English East India Company' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: hees104.txt lines 67-110 (English East India Company, Madras Bombay and Calcutta), 400-475)

concepts.title: Battle of Plassey and Company Rule

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Battle of Plassey and Company Rule' refers to.
questions.a: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 gave the English company control over Bengal's riches, and victories that followed - Buxar and the annexation of Punjab - step by step converted commercial footholds into direct colonial rule over India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Battle of Plassey and Company Rule'.
questions.a: Plassey 1757 is the hinge: from revenue-rich Bengal the company annexed India province by province.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Battle of Plassey and Company Rule' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Life under Colonial Rule: Portuguese Rule and Europeans in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Life under Colonial Rule: Portuguese Rule and Europeans in India' refers to.
questions.a: Colonialism reshaped Indian life: the Portuguese enforced religious policies in their enclaves, European settlements changed coastal cities, and exploitative land taxes and trade rules drained Indian wealth while drawing India into a world empire.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Life under Colonial Rule: Portuguese Rule and Europeans in India'.
questions.a: Colonial rule meant political control plus economic drain and cultural pressure.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Life under Colonial Rule: Portuguese Rule and Europeans in India' taught, and from which source text?
